open_questions: Why QLP sector 91 depth 20667 +/-2455 ppm is much deeper than TESS-SPOC 7189 +/-1058 ppm - coexisting spot modulation vs pipeline dilution calibration on this active M dwarf with 13671-23661 ppm variability
True transit duration offset (observed 1.999 h vs central 2.059 h) and 3.45 vs 3.69 Re planet size depend on TIC 0.3206 Rsun vs Gaia FLAME 0.3428 Rsun host radii
Centroid on-target remains to be formally confirmed (centroid_all not_run / inconclusive) pending higher-SNR difference imaging, though neighbour limit 0 within 1px already rules out plausible blend
dossier.public_summary: A ~13.3-day, ~9686 ppm flat-bottom dip on an M dwarf implies a 3.5 Earth-radius transiting companion with a planet-like 2-hour duration; huge spot variability and pipeline depth differences make the signal look noisy but the shape, duration and lack of any nearby star that could mimic the dip together make a planet the best explanation.

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed, near-central duration for the host (TIC 0.321 Rsun, Gaia FLAME 0.343 Rsun: durations 0.97 and 0.91 of central) and size 3.45 Re (3.69 Re at FLAME radius) below the giant-planet limit; positively favours a transiting planet on the target over a V-shaped grazing EB.

No star inside one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can produce the 9686 ppm dip with a plausible eclipse (0% <=25% needed), contralow contamination and low ruwe 1.021, ruling out a deep eclipsing neighbour; centroid is inconclusive but not off-target, so a blended EB requires an implausibly deep and distant eclipse.

reasons.why: Modest odd/even and secondary differences far below the 4-sigma/5-sigma thresholds for a real binary at twice the 13.3 d period and beyond best brightening, and while light curves show huge spot variability (amplitude 13671-23661 ppm) the transit shape is boxy (v_sigma -2.527) not sinusoidal/phase-curve dominated, weighing against the stellar-variability/EB explanations despite the scorer's low rank.

reasons.why: Apparent 131.9% depth change and inconsistent single transits are driven by different light-curve products (cross-source calibration per rules) and one strong outlier only affecting the top-three share; within TESS-SPOC the two depths are consistent within errors, so no intrinsic on-target depth change requiring a false-positive, recognising the tool says QLP depth 20715 vs SPOC mean 7189 ppm differs technically but is expected between pipelines, not astrophysical.
